groups.name: Theory & methods
groups.blurb: Models, proofs and the tools for testing them.

groups.name: Macroeconomics & international
groups.blurb: Whole economies and the links between them.

groups.name: Labor, people & public policy
groups.blurb: Work, households and what governments do.

groups.name: Development, space & environment
groups.blurb: Poor countries, cities, land and nature.

groups.name: Institutions, history & ideas
groups.blurb: Politics, law, the past and the discipline itself.

areas.name: Microeconomic theory
areas.blurb: Choice, markets and information: the core theory of how individuals and firms decide.

areas.name: Game theory & market design
areas.blurb: Strategic interaction, from equilibrium concepts to auctions, matching and mechanism design.

areas.name: Behavioral & experimental economics
areas.blurb: How people actually choose: psychology, social preferences and evidence from the lab and the field.

areas.name: Econometrics & quantitative methods
areas.blurb: The statistical toolkit of the discipline: identification, estimation, time series and forecasting.

areas.name: Macroeconomics
areas.blurb: Business cycles, consumption, investment, unemployment and fiscal policy in the aggregate economy.

areas.name: Monetary economics & central banking
areas.blurb: Money, inflation and how central banks set and transmit policy.

areas.name: Economic growth & productivity
areas.blurb: Why some economies grow rich: capital, ideas, productivity and structural change over the long run.

areas.name: International trade
areas.blurb: Why countries trade, who gains and loses, and how policy and firms shape global commerce.

areas.name: International finance & open-economy macro
areas.blurb: Exchange rates, capital flows, currency crises and sovereign debt in a connected world economy.

areas.name: Asset pricing & financial markets
areas.blurb: How risk is priced: portfolios, market efficiency, derivatives, liquidity and investor behavior.

areas.name: Corporate finance & governance
areas.blurb: How firms raise money, pay it out and are controlled: capital structure, governance and deals.

areas.name: Banking, intermediation & financial crises
areas.blurb: What banks do, how they are regulated and why financial systems periodically break down.

areas.name: Monopoly & market power
areas.blurb: Monopoly, oligopoly, antitrust and regulation: the original 6,185-paper bibliography.

areas.name: Firms, organizations & entrepreneurship
areas.blurb: Why firms exist and how they are run: boundaries, incentives, management and new ventures.

areas.name: Innovation, technology & the digital economy
areas.blurb: Where new ideas come from, how they spread, and how digital technology changes markets.

areas.name: Labor economics
areas.blurb: Work and pay: human capital, wages, job search, discrimination, migration and unions.

areas.name: Economics of education
areas.blurb: What makes schools and universities work, and how skills are formed from early childhood on.

areas.name: Health economics
areas.blurb: Health as an economic good: behavior, insurance, providers and the value of medical care.

areas.name: Public economics
areas.blurb: Taxes, transfers and public goods: what governments do and how people respond.

areas.name: Inequality, poverty & mobility
areas.blurb: Who gets what: the distribution of income and wealth, poverty and chances across generations.

areas.name: Population, family & gender
areas.blurb: Households as economic units: fertility, marriage, gender roles and aging.

areas.name: Development economics
areas.blurb: How poor countries and poor households get by and get ahead: credit, risk, schooling, health and aid.

areas.name: Urban, regional & spatial economics
areas.blurb: Why economic activity clusters in cities, and what that means for housing, land and transport.

areas.name: Environmental, energy & resource economics
areas.blurb: Pricing pollution, valuing nature and managing energy, climate and natural resources.

areas.name: Agricultural & food economics
areas.blurb: Farms, food and rural land: production, policy, prices and what ends up on the plate.

areas.name: Political economy & institutions
areas.blurb: How politics shapes economic outcomes: voting, interest groups, institutions, conflict and reform.

areas.name: Law & economics
areas.blurb: The economic logic of legal rules: property, liability, contracts, crime and the courts.

areas.name: Economic history
areas.blurb: How economies actually developed: industrialization, crises, empires and living standards over centuries.

areas.name: History of economic thought & methodology
areas.blurb: Where economic ideas came from, the schools that fought over them, and how economists reason.

areas.name: Culture, media & society
areas.blurb: Economics beyond markets: culture and trust, religion, the news media and the arts.
